title: Should the Navigation menu page be about the mega menu only?
context: The page is the mega menu (MegaMenu: a top item that opens a big panel of links). Its written purpose and keyboard text still describe the side list (NavList rows with counts, pins and folding groups), a different component.

current.text: A top navigation item that opens a large panel of grouped links. It is a disclosure (a button with aria-expanded and a panel of headings and lists of links), not a menu.
Lists the places in a side navigation, such as folders or settings sections, with counts, collapsible groups and pins.
Rows, subgroup rows and pin buttons are native links and buttons reached with Tab, activated with Enter (and Space for buttons). It adds no arrow key handling.

current.text: Moves between the sections of one page or the subpages of one area, with in-page links or a table of contents that marks where you are.

context: The spec and code say that on a phone the pane is a bottom bar plus its own screen, never a drawer. The written purpose now says so; an older guidance line still says “overlay on small screens”.

current.text: Gives every page the same left pane for moving around inside an application, collapsible to a rail; on medium windows it opens over the page, and on a phone it becomes a bottom bar and a screen of its own, never a drawer.
Narrow (under 600px): a bottom navigation bar of the page's destinations (or a parent row) and the pane as a screen of its own, never a drawer (Platforms Standard 4.1).
